title: LIFEPLAN Malaise sample metabarcoding
author: Jeremy R. deWaard
materials: Pooling PCR2 product The PCR2 products labeled with P5/P7 Illumina indexing adapters were checked by running 4 µL of the product on the Invitrogen pre-cast E-Gel 2% agarose gel for 00:04:00 . An equal volume of each sample ( 6 µL ) was pooled into one 96-well microplate using an Biomek i7 Automated Liquid Handling Workstation (Beckman Coulter LIfe Sciences, Indianapolis) robot. The pooled PCR products were then transferred into a 5 – 15 mL tube. Figure 9. Pooling of 12 96-well PCR2 plates into a single 96-well microplate using an Biomek i7 Automated Liquid Handling Workstation.

Size selection To target the desired length of amplicons, and thereby eliminate non-specific, especially long fragments of DNA from the DNA library, we used an Invitrogen Size-Select 2% agarose gel, according to the protocol recommended by the manufacturer. The final volume of the target DNA was approximately 200 µL .

Final purification and evaluation of the quality of the DNA library The volume of the target DNA library was evaluated by using a Rainin pipette (Mettler Toledo, Mississauga, ON). The 0.8 ratio of Cytiva magnetic beads:pooled library was applied. For library concentration, we used the standard recommendations of the manufacturer, including 00:08:00 on the bench at Room temperature , 00:02:00 on the magnet, four washes with 1 mL of 80% freshly prepared ethanol, elution with 23 µL of water, and collecting 20 µL . To evaluate the concentration of the final DNA library, we used the Qubit High Sensitivity kit reagents and the Qubit 2.0 Fluorometer (Invitrogen). The normalized 1 ng/uL concentration of the final library was checked on the Bioanalyzer (Agilent Technology, Santa Clara) using the High Sensitivity kit in order to visualize the length of the target DNA. Figure 10. The concentration of the final DNA library read using a Qubit 2.0 Fluorometer (Invitrogen)

PCR1 reactions were carried out with the following thermocycler settings: initial denaturation at 95 °C for 00:05:00 , 30 cycles of denaturation at 94 °C for 00:00:30 , annealing at 46 °C for 00:00:30 , extension at 72 °C for 00:00:50 , and lastly extension for 00:05:00 at 72 °C . A 2 µL volume of DNA template and AMPtk positive control were added to corresponding wells. The microplate of genomic DNA was heat-sealed and archived at -80 °C for future use. First-round PCR products were diluted by 1x before the second round of PCR.

PCR2 reactions employed fusion versions of BF3 and BR2 primers tailed with one of 24 6- to 10-base long in-line tags and P5 or P7 sequencing adaptors (Illumina) for a total of 1152 unique combinations of tag pairs. The total number of unique combinations factors in half of the samples being sequenced in reverse direction by swapping P5 and P7 tails on the indexed primers. PCR2 reactions were carried out with the following thermocycler settings: initial denaturation at 94 °C for 00:02:00 , 15 cycles of denaturation at 94 °C for 00:00:40 , annealing at 51 °C for 00:01:00 , extension at 72 °C for 00:01:00 , and lastly extension for 00:05:00 at 72 °C . A 2 µL volume of PCR1 template, including positive and negative controls, was added.

steps.title: Sample Preservation
steps.instruction: Preserve insect specimens in fresh 96% ethanol and store at -20 °C until processing.

steps.title: Ethanol Filtration and Biomass Measurement
steps.instruction: Filter ethanol from bulk samples to determine wet arthropod biomass using a vacuum manifold.

substeps.instruction: Tare the weight of five Microfunnel 0.45 uM Supor membrane filters (Pall Laboratory) using an analytic and precision weighing balance (Sartorius) and place them on a 6-Funnel vacuum manifold (Pall Laboratory).
Filter the bulk insect specimens through the membranes until all specimens are transferred and all ethanol is removed.
Weigh the membrane and specimen contents, subtracting the initial tared weight to calculate the wet arthropod biomass.
Transfer the specimen contents and membrane back into the bulk sample bottle for lysis.

steps.title: Tissue Lysis
steps.instruction: Lysis of insect specimens using a specific volume of insect lysis buffer based on biomass.

substeps.instruction: Determine the volume of insect lysis buffer (700 mM GuSCN, 30 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 30 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 0.5% Triton X-100, and 5% Tween20) based on wet weight: 0-9.9g: 50mL; 10-19.9g: 100mL; 20-29.9g: 200mL; 30-39.9g: 300mL; 40-49.9g: 400mL; 50-59.9g: 500mL; 60-69.9g: 600mL; 70-79.9g: 700mL; 80-100g: 800mL.
Add the buffer to the bulk bottle, ensuring all specimens are submerged.
Incubate samples on a rotating shaker (VWR) at 56 °C overnight.

Take three technical replicates of 300 µL aliquots of lysate from each sample and transfer them to a 500 µL 96-well deep well plate (Eppendorf), including three negative (template-free) and three positive (AMPtk synthetic) controls per block.

steps.title: DNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract DNA using a membrane-based protocol with a glass fiber plate.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL of lysate from each well to a microplate (archive the remaining 250 µL).
Add 100 µL of binding mix (50 mL 96% ethanol mixed with 50 mL Binding Buffer [6 M GuSCN, 20 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 6.4, 4% Triton X-100, pre-warmed at 56 °C]) to the lysate.
Mix the 150 µL total volume and transfer to a 3.0 µm Pall Supor Membrane glass fiber plate; centrifuge at 5000 x g at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add 180 µL of protein wash buffer (70 mL 96% ethanol mixed with 26 mL Binding Buffer) and centrifuge at 5000 x g at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Perform two additional washes using 600 µL of wash buffer (60% ethanol, 50 mM NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 0.5 mM EDTA pH 8.0), centrifuging at 5000 x g at room temperature for 5 minutes each.
Place the glass fiber plate onto a new DNA storage microplate and incubate at 56 °C for 30 minutes.
Add 60 µL of elution buffer, incubate at room temperature for 1 minute, and centrifuge at 5000 x g for 5 minutes to elute DNA.

steps.title: PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify a 418 bp region of cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) using two rounds of PCR.

substeps.instruction: Perform PCR1 using forward primer BF3 and reverse primer BR2.
Perform PCR2 to add P5/P7 Illumina adapters.
Use a Beckman Coulter Biomek FX P automated workstation for DNA and PCR product transfers.

steps.title: DNA Library Concentration
steps.instruction: Concentrate the pooled DNA library using magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Use a 0.8–1.2 ratio of magnetic beads (Cytiva Sera-Mag Carboxylate-Modified Magnetic SpeedBeads) to pooled PCR product.
Prepare four 1.5 mL Eppendorf LoBind tubes with 160 µL of magnetic beads each.
Vortex the pooled DNA library and add 200 µL to each tube.
Incubate on the bench at room temperature for 8 minutes, then on the magnet for 2 minutes.
Perform three washes with 1 mL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol.
Elute with 45 µL of water and collect 40 µL from each tube (total volume 160 µL).

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the library on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform.

substeps.instruction: Use the S Prime (SP) reagent kit, SP flow cell, and 500-cycle configuration.
Load each lane with its own library containing 1152 dual-indexed amplicons.
Configure for 2x258bp paired-end sequencing (redirecting indexing flows to the insert).
Include up to 15% PhiX spike-in for base diversity.

steps.title: Bioinformatics and Taxonomic Assignment
steps.instruction: Process sequencing reads using mBRAVE for filtering, clustering, and assignment.

substeps.instruction: Demultiplex reads and upload to mBRAVE.
Trim 23 bp from both termini and disable primer masking.
Filter reads: minimum length >446 bp, mean QV > 20, <6% positions with QV < 20, and <1% positions with QV < 10.
Pre-cluster into OTUs (threshold = 3%; minimum size = 1 read).

Query OTUs against ten BOLD system libraries (SYS-MBRAVEC, SYS-CRLBACTERIA, SYS-CRLNONARTHINVERT, SYS-CRLNONINSECTARTH, SYS-CRLINSECTA, SYS-CRLCHORDATA, SYS-CRLAVES, SYS-CRLPROTISTA, and SYS-HUMC) with an ID distance threshold of 2% and minimum overlap of 100bp.
Generate BIN tables in Excel; subtract read counts of BINs found in negative controls from non-control wells and discard bacterial, protist, and other contaminant reads.
